output.name: Varesk
output.myth: Varesk was a fishing boat out of the north skerries, and her crew were quarrelsome and short of salt. One autumn they sailed south to trade for rope, and Tavo the Gale came down on them like a dropped sack. Mast and sail went, and the water came over the gunwale. The youngest kept a lamp lit in the bow, and the others went out one by one. Kael the Netter cast for her and never caught her, because a lamp is hard to net. Sil saw the light from the moon and called down to Aun, who said nothing, as he does when guilty. Lavesk, the Drying Shag, saw it too, and its wives set the kettle on and waited. Ulkun, the salt pot the sky keeps, holds a pinch of that crew's salt. Mirhan, the gull who lost a word, sees it from the west and cannot name it. So the boat is still out there, sailing the Upper Sea with her two lamps lit. If you see a light low in the south, do not wave. Mend your net and go to bed.
output.finding: From Lavesk, the Drying Shag, low in the south, go one fist (about 10°) south-east and look for the light of Varesk.
